title: We Are South Maui: Community Plan Advisory Committee Meeting of March 15, 2023

issues.title: MEMA community resiliency hub network plan
Using recycled R1 water for irrigation and firefighting

recap.headline: South Maui plan committee finishes resiliency actions and revises wetland purchase goal
recap.in_60_seconds: The South Maui Community Plan Advisory Committee met on March 15, 2023 to keep drafting actions for the South Maui Community Plan. No members of the public testified. Remote testimony was still not available, and the meeting was not streamed on Akaka. About 12 committee members and 2 Planning Department staff spoke. The committee voted to call for the County to acquire seven North Kīhei parcels it sees as wetlands and to protect them as open space. It also adopted actions on wildfire data, a new fire station in North Kīhei, evacuation routes and gate blockages, resiliency hubs, native and canoe plants, recycled water, water reuse and desalination studies, and drought planning, and it finished the resiliency section. Whether the seven parcels are legally wetlands is still open; staff said a County wetland map is due around October or November.

parts.title: Call to order and housekeeping
presented: Roll call at 5:30 p.m.; all members present.
Still no live streaming on Akaka and no remote testimony; the meeting was streamed on the Kīhei Community Association website and Facebook page.
A member disclosed that three committee members joined a Kīhei Community Association design review walk-through of ranch land; no committee business was discussed.

parts.title: Revisiting the wetland and flood-prone parcel acquisition action
parts.presenter: Committee member who made the motion
presented: A member moved to change last week's adopted text from 'flood-prone parcels' to acquiring wetlands on seven listed North Kīhei parcels, about 1.1 to 7 acres each, and protecting them as open space in perpetuity.
Members argued that Ordinance 5421 protects wetlands and allows them to be acquired, but says nothing about flood-prone land.
Some members worried the wording was too broad, could cost a lot, and could cover large parts of Kīhei; the word 'purchase' was changed to 'acquire' so donations and exchanges are included.
A second action was adopted separately: explore conservation easements or acquisition of wetlands, gulches, streams and floodplains, based on the wetland mapping study and other studies.

answered.said: The contract for the County wetland map is being executed, with notice to proceed around now; the map should be ready around October or November, 365 days after the ordinance took effect October 4.
If the mayor puts a parcel in the capital budget, the department would compare it against the wetland map, though there may be other reasons to buy land outside the map.
State law already requires realtors to disclose sea level rise risk to buyers.

parts.title: Sea level rise, shoreline access and wildfire actions (3.07 to 3.10)
presented: Adopted an inventory of natural and cultural resources affected by sea level rise.
Adopted staff's revised shoreline access language, including relocating coastal trails.
Adopted an update of the 2016 South Maui Community Wildfire Protection Plan, with enforcement that developments and landowners comply.
Adopted a wildfire data set that records cause, acreage, year and location, and adds prevention recommendations.

parts.title: New fire station and disaster planning (3.11 and 3.12)
presented: Adopted a new action to build a fire station mauka of Pi’ilani Highway in the North Kīhei area, outside sea level rise and tsunami zones.
Adopted a community-based disaster preparedness plan and a long-term post-disaster recovery plan.

answered.said: Planners worked with the fire chief on the fire station wording; keeping the location broad lets the Fire Department find land.
The recovery plan is meant to make disaster planning proactive rather than reactive.

parts.title: Evacuation routes and blocked exits (3.13 and new action)
presented: Adopted an action to identify more evacuation routes in and out of South Maui and to share them through many communication channels.
A member said ranches have agreed to provide emergency routes.
Adopted a new action to find and remove gates and other blockages to evacuation in areas with limited exits, with a plan to open them in an emergency.
Members described dead-end streets such as Hauʻoli Street in Māʻalaea, where people may have to drive toward a tsunami to get out.

next.what: Committee returns to the transportation section

parts.title: Resiliency hubs and native plantings (3.14, 3.15 and new action)
presented: Adopted an action to create resiliency hubs for South Maui.
A member said FEMA has reviewed school cafeterias as hubs, with generators and solar planned.
Adopted an action to identify roadsides for native trees and ground cover to reduce disaster risk.
Adopted a new action on native agroforestry and canoe plants for food security and practical materials, with a long-term zero-waste plan.

answered.said: Defined resiliency hubs as community facilities set up to support residents and share resources before, during and after disasters.

next.what: Invite a speaker on food security

parts.title: Capital projects, recycled water and recycling center (3.16 to 3.18)
presented: Deleted 3.16 on prioritizing resilient capital projects as too broad and already required.
Adopted 3.17 on recycled water, changed to focus on converting the largest potable water users, and expanding storage and lines.
Deleted 3.18 on moving the Kīhei recycling and redemption center, since the park expansion that would displace it is decades away.

answered.said: The budget and capital improvement program must already be consistent with community plans under Chapter 2.80B of the Maui County Code.

parts.title: Water reuse, desalination and drought plan (3.19 and 3.20)
presented: The committee voted to split 3.19 into two studies.
Adopted a study of treating recycled water to drinking quality.
Adopted a separate study of a modern desalination facility.
Adopted 3.20: update the drought management plan with the State Department of Land and Natural Resources.

answered.said: Treating wastewater for reuse is the Department of Environmental Management's job, while a desalination study would fit the Department of Water Supply.
DLNR coordinates and gets input on county drought plans; the county does most of the work.

parts.title: Resiliency section closed and adjournment
presented: No more actions were offered; Topic 3, resiliency, was finished.
Adjourned at 8:59 p.m.

bills.name: Ordinance 5421 (County wetlands ordinance)
bills.what: Defines wetlands by their functions and lets the Conservation Planning Committee advise the mayor to acquire wetlands or seek conservation easements.

bills.name: 2016 South Maui Community Wildfire Protection Plan
bills.what: Existing wildfire plan for South Maui that the committee wants updated and enforced.

bills.name: MEMA hazard mitigation plan
bills.what: Emergency management plan to be considered in a community-based disaster preparedness plan.

bills.name: Chapter 2.80B, Maui County Code
bills.what: Requires county budgets and capital programs to be consistent with community plans.

bills.name: Drought management plan
bills.what: County drought plan to be updated with the State Department of Land and Natural Resources.

open_questions.question: Will the seven North Kīhei parcels be officially mapped as wetlands under the County wetland ordinance?
What would it cost the County to acquire the wetland parcels?
Who would build and fund a wildfire GIS data set if the fire chief says it is not needed?
Who decides whether gates blocking evacuation routes, such as near Hauʻoli Street in Māʻalaea, can be opened in an emergency?

not_on_tracker.topic: Acquiring North Kīhei wetland parcels as open space
not_on_tracker.why: Members said these lands carry stormwater and their loss has caused flooding in North Kīhei neighborhoods.

not_on_tracker.topic: Blocked evacuation exits in dead-end neighborhoods
not_on_tracker.why: Residents of areas like Hauʻoli Street in Māʻalaea may have only one way out in a fire or tsunami.

not_on_tracker.topic: New fire station in North Kīhei
not_on_tracker.why: The current Kīhei station is in the sea level rise zone and far from growing northern areas.

not_on_tracker.topic: Treating recycled water to drinking quality
not_on_tracker.why: It could add a new South Maui water source but faces public acceptance concerns.

moments.quote: One of our assignments is to create a wetlands map, and we are executing the contract for that.
moments.about: Planning staff said a contract for a South Maui wetlands map was starting, with results expected that fall, to inform the plan's wetland acquisition action.

moments.who: A South Maui Community Plan Advisory Committee member from Kīhei
moments.quote: The climate change, those houses near Halama Street and Mauka of Halama Street, they are all experiencing nature's wetland. It's happening.
moments.about: A committee member described flooding near Halama Street to explain why the plan calls for acquiring and protecting South Maui wetlands.

moments.who: A South Maui Community Plan Advisory Committee member
moments.quote: And they said, at least in a tsunami, we have no way out. We have to go towards the tsunami to get out.
moments.about: A committee member relayed residents' long-standing concern about blocked roads, which led to a plan action to identify and remove impediments to evacuation.
